title: DevExp SDK Pathfinder — Sprint Blueprint
content:
Purpose:
A compact, hands-on sprint blueprint to validate a single-day SDK onboarding flow that any engineer can run through and ship a mini-integration. This is intentionally lightweight: goal is a repeatable learning loop (learn -> build -> measure -> iterate) that feeds into the main SDK quickstart and example repos.

Intended audience:
- New engineers and integrators evaluating Redwood SDKs (JS/Python)
- Developer advocates running 60/90 min demo labs
- Solutions engineers doing pilot workshops

Primary outcomes (Sprint-level):
- One reproducible, instrumented mini-integration that covers auth, simple generation call, streaming, error handling, and telemetry.
- A 20–30 minute guided lab script and a 10-minute self-serve sandbox path.
- Telemetry checklist + lightweight assertions for flakiness and latency that can be run automatically.

Success metrics (what we measure):
- Time-to-first-successful-call (target median <= 8 minutes for a first-time user in the sandbox)
- % of participants who finish the guided lab without needing 1:1 help (target >= 80%)
- Telemetry pass rate for sample traffic (no more than 5% error responses under nominal conditions)
- Qualitative satisfaction score from lab survey (target >= 4/5)

Sprint length and cadence:
- 2-week exploratory sprint (prototype in week 1, pilot with 5 internal testers in week 2)
- Daily sync: 15 min at 10:30 for blockers/check-ins

Curriculum modules (ordered minimal path):
1) Welcome + quick context (5 mins)
   - What the SDKs solve, high-level product terms (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
   - Expectations for the mini-integration
2) Setup & auth (10 mins)
   - Install JS or Python SDK, env var + token pattern, local sandbox token instructions
   - Troubleshooting common local issues (firewalls, proxy)
3) Hello-gen (10 mins)
   - Make the first generation call (sync), inspect response shape, discuss tokens and cost
4) Streaming + partial output (10 mins)
   - Hook a streaming callback to progressively render tokens; checklist for UX fallbacks
5) Tooling & error-handling (10 mins)
   - Retry/backoff example, idempotency keys, graceful fallback to smaller model variant
6) Telemetry sanity checks (10 mins)
   - Collect latency, error codes, model id; run quick assertions against expected thresholds
7) Mini feature: add a prompt template and a small reranking step (15 mins)
   - Show where to plug in Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching/quantization hinting)
8) Wrap + demo checklist (5 mins)

Labs (deliverables):
- Lab A: Sandbox Quickstart (single-file example that runs locally)
- Lab B: Streaming chat UI stub (React/Vite minimal)
- Lab C: Instrumented smoke test (script that hits the same endpoint with sample traces and verifies telemetry)

Required assets for pilot:
- repo: github.com/redwood-inference/mini-pathfinder-starters (stubbed)
- 3 sandbox tokens for internal testing (provisioned via dev sandbox queue)
- Confluence page (for follow-up) + short survey link
- Short slide deck for 5-min context intro

Telemetry and instrumentation (minimal):
- Events to emit: sdk.start, sdk.first_response, sdk.stream_started, sdk.error, sdk.end
- Metrics: median_p10_p50_p90 latency (ms), error_rate, token_count per call
- Assertion thresholds: p90_latency <= 1200 ms for small prompt; error_rate < 5%
- Quick script: run 20 calls, fail sprint if more than 1 call returns 5xx

Rollout plan for quickstart artifacts:
- Day 3: merge starter repo with one-file examples and smoke test
- Day 7: run internal pilot with 5 engineers, collect notes and telemetry
- Day 10: adjust lab script + reduce friction points (auth, install, env)
- Day 14: publicize via developer-newsletter and attach to onboarding flow

Gating criteria for promoting from draft -> public quickstart:
- >= 5 successful internal runs with telemetry assertions satisfied
- Lab script reduced to <= 25 steps and time-to-first-successful-call median <= 8 minutes
- A short troubleshooting FAQ addressing top 3 failure modes observed during pilot

Sample timeline for a 1-hour workshop (for advocates):
- 00:00–05:00: Intro + goals + token setup (in parallel)
- 05:00–20:00: Hello-gen + explain response shape + tokens/cost
- 20:00–35:00: Streaming UI lab (pair exercise)
- 35:00–45:00: Error-handling & telemetry demo
- 45:00–55:00: Mini feature (rerank) + wrap
- 55:00–60:00: Survey + next steps

Known friction points (notes to self):
- Local networking + corp VPN often block streaming websockets -> provide HTTP fallback sample and clear docs
- Token confusion: users attempt to use production tokens in sandbox. Add explicit token naming guidance in README
- Dependency version mismatch across starter repos -> lock versions and provide one-click npx / pipx entrypoint if possible

Open questions (to resolve in week 1):
- Do we want to default to a model variant that is lowest-cost but guarantees latency? (tradeoff with output quality)
- Should the sandbox token expire after X hours to avoid leaking state? Ops input needed
- Which telemetry platform will we use for pilot ingestion (Lightstep vs existing console)?

Demo checklist (for the person running the lab):
- [ ] Starter repo cloned and dependencies installed
- [ ] Sandbox tokens provisioned and set in env
- [ ] Streaming demo confirmed behind corp firewall (or fallback in place)
- [ ] Smoke test script passes locally (20 calls)
- [ ] Survey link ready for participants

Next steps / owners:
- Evan W.: scaffold starter repo + minimal README + smoke test (due Day 3)
- Priya N.: author 1-hour workshop script and slides (due Day 5)
- Luca: provision 3 sandbox tokens and quick provisioning checklist (due Day 2)
- Sofia: run pilot sessions with infra and collect telemetry (Days 7–9)

Notes and tone guidance for final quickstart page:
- Keep language pragmatic and action-first: "Run this, see output, change this"
- Surface cost and latency tradeoffs inline near examples (inline comments)
- Provide a clear "If X fails, try Y" troubleshooting block after each step

Links & references:
- Slack: #devexp-sprint-pathfinder (live coordination)
- GitHub draft: github.com/redwood-inference/mini-pathfinder-starters (WIP)
- Confluence draft: CON-9876 (lab notes)

Quick personal reflections (informal):
- Aim for the smallest possible friction that still teaches the right mental model for integrating with Redwood: auth -> call -> stream -> telemetry. If users leave with that, we win.
- Keep the labs bite-sized so we can reuse pieces for workshops, docs, and partner enablement.
